scope: Operating-system foundation, Mora desktop shell, native services and federated source workspace.

reference.warning: The supplied 66-point list mixes cumulative updates, inherited behavior, absence statements, repeated topics and Windows-specific constraints. It is not treated as an authoritative XP SP3 changelog or as a requirement to reproduce legacy Windows behavior.

adoption_rules.rule: Only claim implemented when repository code and tests or operational evidence support the exact behavior. Partial requires evidence and explicit limits. Not applicable requires a product-scope reason. Historical Windows features are not silently represented as native capabilities.

source_groups.title: User interface, shell, multimedia and storage

controls.assessment: Capability contracts and deny-by-default shell preferences exist; kernel-enforced privilege separation and native security-service enforcement remain incomplete.
limitations: Do not treat browser preferences or policy files as OS enforcement.

controls.assessment: The XP reference describes Windows-specific protocol, NAP and IPsec behavior. Dak network-stack parity has not been established; no XP-compatible network implementation is claimed.
limitations: Assess native network stack and adapter policy only after its implementation boundary is defined.

controls.assessment: Deterministic component bundles and deployment plans exist; a bootable installer, physical-disk deployment and complete A/B boot rollback are not claimed.
limitations: Keep image creation and privileged installation separate from planning and archive verification.

controls.assessment: Mora includes a Qt 6 Widgets host-native desktop application with host-managed top-level windows, a local app catalogue, native host input/focus and bounded local panels, while retaining the older browser shell as a reference preview. It is not a Dak kernel compositor, privileged launcher, Windows Explorer replacement or full OS storage stack.
limitations: The Qt app runs under the host OS and is not launched by the Stage 1 Dak kernel.
The kernel compositor, process model, VFS, app sandbox and native capability enforcement remain pending.
Browser-preview behavior must not be represented as kernel-native operation.

controls.assessment: Windows/Linux inspection and pinned source federation exist; native execution compatibility, modern driver coverage and bootable release lifecycle remain partial.
limitations: Keep inspected formats, prepared launch plans and actually executed workloads distinct.
